gaps.sentence: I ___ the dentist on Thursday afternoon — I booked it last week.
gaps.explanation: A personal arrangement already made takes the present continuous: am seeing.

gaps.sentence: When I came downstairs, the whole house ___ of fresh bread.
gaps.hint: smell as a state verb in past
gaps.explanation: 'Smell' as a state verb takes simple tenses, here the past simple: smelled.

gaps.sentence: There ___ a cinema on this corner, but it closed years ago.
gaps.hint: a past state that has ended
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' is also used for past states that no longer exist: used to be.

gaps.sentence: I ___ that film three times, and I would happily watch it again.
gaps.hint: life experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Experience up to the present with no specific past time takes the present perfect: have seen.

gaps.sentence: When I was a boy, films ___ in black and white.
gaps.hint: a past state no longer existing
gaps.explanation: 'Used to be' describes a past state that has ended: used to be.

gaps.sentence: Don't phone between seven and eight — we ___ dinner then.
gaps.hint: in progress at a stated future time
gaps.explanation: Something in progress at a stated future time takes the future continuous: will be having.

gaps.sentence: By the age of thirty, she ___ her own company.
gaps.hint: by the age of means completed before
gaps.explanation: An achievement completed before a past reference point takes the past perfect: had started.

gaps.sentence: I ___ it matters whether we leave at six or seven — the traffic will be terrible either way.
gaps.hint: think meaning believe is a state verb
gaps.explanation: 'Think' in the sense of 'believe' is a state verb, so the negative present simple is used: don't think.
